parts: Please read the continuation note /shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/FINITE_EULER_WEIL_COMPARISON_CONTINUATION_20261003 and proceed with the suggested next steps
I’ll read the continuation note and repository guidance, then work through the suggested next steps.

The note sets a bounded first task: verify the finite-product identity or identify a precise obstruction, then save a derivation and an adversarial audit before changing the manuscript. I’m splitting the checks across transport, trace algebra, and the earlier comparison results.

The finite-product checks so far support the identity at \(\sigma=1/2\), including the inverse metric and smoothed traces. There is also a useful obstruction: \(K\le0\) fails on the full pole-neutral source class when the prime set is held fixed. That leaves the support-adapted comparison open, but rules out an all-support induction starting from that sign claim.

The derivation now gives \(Q[F]=B_{S,1/2}[F]-K_{S,1/2}[F]\) once \(S\) contains every active prime, with the same residual signs as the earlier audit. I’m checking the proposed next inequality carefully: a renamed version of \(Q\ge0\) would not advance the argument.

The identity and sign obstruction are saved, and the adversarial check found no defect in either proof. The next proposed test is a rank-one bound controlled by the source’s mean, modeled on the known short-support archimedean result. It remains unproved; the note spells out why the extra mean-zero condition is allowed by Weil’s criterion and why a one-prime result alone would not suffice.

Completed the first investigation and saved the [derivation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/FINITE_EULER_BOUNDARY_IDENTITY_20261003.md) and [adversarial audit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/reviews/FINITE_EULER_BOUNDARY_AUDIT_20261003.md).

- **Identity verified internally:** \(B_{S,\sigma}=\Gamma-W_{S,\sigma}+K_{S,\sigma}\) for every finite \(S\), \(\sigma>0\), and compact smooth complex source, retaining the inverse metric and justified trace operations.
- **Obstruction proved:** expanding pole-neutral sources give \(K_{S,\sigma}>B_{S,\sigma}\) for every fixed finite \(S\). This does not refute the support-adapted comparison.
- **Next inequality specified:** a rank-one bound controlled by the source’s mean, beginning with \(S=\{2\}\) and support length \(1\). It remains unproved.

The residual signs agree with the earlier audit. Support-adapted positivity remains open; the manuscript was not changed.
Please modify the manuscript with the new results, citing the note for detailed calculations. Then please continue with investigating the unresolved items.

I’ll add the finite-product identity and fixed-place obstruction to the manuscript, citing the detailed note. Then I’ll investigate the proposed rank-one bound, starting with prime \(2\) and support length \(1\).

The manuscript additions are drafted. I also found that the mean-only bound and its abstract Schur criterion were already proposed in the September notes, so I’m treating them as prior work. The new investigation is focused on evaluating the actual boundary resolvent, with bounds for the parts omitted by a finite approximation.

The revised manuscript compiles successfully in the built-in editor. The first boundary computations show a positive correction for an exactly mean-zero odd source, which could refute the proposed rank-one bound. The values still change with refinement, so this is only an exploratory signal. I’m checking the omitted-space error before drawing a sign conclusion.

The computations exposed an important approximation error: the boundary matrix is \(I-E^*C^2E\), whereas using \(I-(E^*CE)^2\) omits a positive contribution from outside the trial space. Keeping that term changes the numerical correction substantially. I’ve derived and audited bounds for this omitted contribution and the full residuals; the correction’s sign is still uncertified.

Updated the [manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/manuscript.tex) with the finite Euler identity, support-adapted comparison, and fixed-place obstruction, citing the detailed note. **Compilation succeeded.**

The continued investigation produced:

- [Full residual error bounds](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/FINITE_EULER_BOUNDARY_RESIDUAL_CERTIFICATE_20261003.md), including source truncation and omitted spatial components.
- Exact formulas showing that the required compressed matrix is \(I-E^*C^2E\); squaring the compressed \(C\) misses a positive contribution.
- A reproducible [first-prime diagnostic](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/numerics/finite_euler_first_prime_DIAGNOSTIC_20261003.md). The mean-zero odd source gives positive approximations, but substantial refinement sensitivity prevents a sign conclusion.

The rank-one bound remains unresolved. The next concrete step is a certified correction enclosure using the new residual bounds.
